title: The month tomato prices jumped across India
summary: In February 2008, the median tomato market moved +40.0% in a month, 4.0 standard deviations from the usual for that month.
why_selected: Chosen automatically: the 4.0σ seasonal move is among the largest on record for tomato, across 245 reporting markets.

evidence.observations: monthly medians of daily modal prices; markets need ≥5 reports in both months
caveats: Many market points are district centres, not mandi gates.
Modal prices are reported aggregates, not transaction offers.

scenes.headline: February 2008
scenes.caption: Tomato prices across 245 markets that reported in both January 2008 and February 2008.

scenes.headline: Median move +40.0%
scenes.caption: The typical market's tomato price jumped 40.0% in one month. 80% of markets moved the same way.

scenes.headline: 4.0× the usual swing
scenes.caption: Compared with the same month in every earlier year on record, this move was 4.0 standard deviations from normal.

scenes.headline: Gujarat
scenes.caption: Neighbouring markets moved together: the 21 reporting markets in Gujarat had a median change of +77.5%.

scenes.headline: Shahabad
scenes.caption: Shahabad (Haryana), one of the busiest markets among the biggest movers: monthly median ₹350 → ₹650 per quintal (+85.7%).

scenes.headline: What this does and doesn't show
scenes.caption: These are reported wholesale modal prices, not causes. Weather, arrivals or policy may explain the move, but this story shows only what markets reported.

conclusion: These are reported wholesale modal prices, not causes. Weather, arrivals or policy may explain the move, but this story shows only what markets reported.
